title: The Atlas of Worlds
subtitle: ca. 1579–1601 IC — The Elder, The Conquerors, The Maven & The Siege

cards.title: The Elder — Child of Decay
cards.text: A creature of malignant madness, born of the oblivion before time. The Elder entered our realm, fashioning a 'bauble' of chaos and secret worlds — the Atlas — as its hunting ground. Preferring young prey, it dragged children into its shadow realm, feasting on their nightmares and imagination. With such sustenance, it sought to cultivate the Decay — the oblivion from outside time and space.
cards.flavorText: "They called it the Elder. A creature of malignant madness, born of that oblivion from before time itself began." — Book of Memories

cards.title: The Watchers of Decay
cards.text: A nameless god of Wraeclast endowed an Azmeri mother — who had lost her child to the Elder — with knowledge of its existence. She founded the Watchers of Decay, a sect of grieving parents who fought the creature. They built the Map Device to travel to its domain and forged Starforge — a blade that could divorce agency from form. They trapped the Elder in stone, starved and unable to hunt. But its essence roamed free...
cards.flavorText: "One by one, they stood their ground against a creature they had no hope of understanding, let alone defeating, and one by one, they became a part of it." — Watcher's Eye

cards.title: Valdo Caeserius & The Shade (1579 IC)
cards.text: Valdo Caeserius, chief Arkhon of the Oriath academy, was ordered by High Templar Venarius to repair a broken golden device found in Wraeclast ruins. While working, Valdo fell asleep and awoke in the Dreamlands — the Atlas. There he met a Shade, the Elder's disembodied spirit, who posed as the rightful king of the realm. The Shade offered help rebuilding the device's missing component in exchange for a future favor.
cards.flavorText: "With the patience of a prowling lion, the Shade watched the Scholar." — Cyclopean Coil

cards.title: The Elder Released
cards.text: When the Shade asked Valdo to pull Starforge from its petrified body, Valdo hesitated and fled. But Venarius, learning of the Dreamlands, took Valdo and his daughter Zana at knifepoint into the Atlas. Venarius pulled the sword without hesitation. The Elder burst free. It consumed Venarius and his men. Valdo fled with Zana through the portal, jammed the Map Device, and went back alone — determined to stop the Elder or die trying.
cards.flavorText: "A single act of love and defiance may cascade destruction across the cosmos." — Cosmic Fragment

cards.title: Zana Caeserius & The Map Device (ca. 1600 IC)
cards.text: Orphaned after Valdo's sacrifice, Zana grew up as an indentured servant. She rediscovered the Map Device during Oriath's rebuilding after Dominus fell. Using it, she entered the Atlas — a realm of dreamlike worlds connected through ancient maps. She discovered her father had become the Shaper, his mind consumed by the Elder, endlessly creating twisted worlds.
cards.flavorText: "I first started exploring the Atlas as a way to grow closer to my estranged father. I had no idea just how close I would get to him..." — Zana

cards.title: Recruiting the Exiles
cards.text: Zana assembled a secret team of exiles: Sirus (leader), Baran (Templar faithful), Al-Hezmin (hunter), Drox (commander), and Veritania (humanitarian). Together they explored the Atlas, pursuing the Shaper and investigating the Elder. The group grew close — Zana and Sirus developed feelings for each other.
cards.flavorText: "Sirus was the leader of the group of Exiles I recruited. Brilliant and determined... We grew close." — Zana

cards.title: The Final Battle Against the Elder
cards.text: Using Valdo's weapon — the Cosmic Arcana — found in his secret study, Zana's group confronted the Elder at the Atlas center. The device forced the Elder from physical form, but it clung to reality. Sirus leapt onto the creature, and both spiraled into the trap, seemingly lost forever. The Elder was sealed, but at the cost of Sirus's life — and Valdo's last memories of Zana.
cards.flavorText: "The Elder fed on all that gave life meaning until it encountered an unbreakable bond." — Decayed Voidstone

cards.title: The Nature of the Atlas
cards.text: The Atlas is not mere geography — it is a dreamlike realm that reflects the desires and expectations of those within it. It offers up your wildest wishes while slowly eroding sanity. The land undulates and shifts, growing seasons of stone, structure, growth, madness, and chaos. Memories echo forever within. Even the dead linger. The Atlas is humanity's greatest defense against eldritch threats — yet also its most dangerous trap.
cards.flavorText: "Like stepping into a dream..." — Duelist, on entering first map

cards.title: Al-Hezmin, The Hunter
cards.text: Al-Hezmin mastered the ever-changing Atlas terrain. But his drive to always be the best — hunting more, striking flashier — consumed him. His fixation hollowed him out, making him desperately afraid of being second best. He was never unkind to Zana, but his rivalry with Drox became inevitable. As madness crept in, he could no longer tell reality from illusion.
cards.flavorText: "Are you even real? I can't tell anymore." — Al-Hezmin

cards.title: Drox, The Warlord
cards.text: The group's battlefield commander, Drox became obsessed with building a kingdom in the Atlas — free from Templar tyranny. But control in the Atlas is an illusion. He grew cold and distant, fixated on securing valleys that reshaped themselves the moment he moved on. His warm grin turned to a scowl as he imagined phantom subjects cheering his golden reign.
cards.flavorText: "Hahaha! Glorious freedom. Violence. Death! This is our promised land!" — Drox

cards.title: Veritania, The Redeemer
cards.text: Originally exiled for her charity work with mistreated Maraketh and Karui, Veritania's clarity of mind was invaluable during the campaign. But her mind broke in a different way — her restraint became contempt. She judged all others as repugnant, filled with vice, and appointed herself the moral heart of the Atlas, purging those she deemed unworthy.
cards.flavorText: "Welcome! Time has no meaning here. Your pain will be endless." — Veritania

cards.title: Baran, The Crusader
cards.text: Despite everything the Templar put him through, Baran's faith was unshaken. He and Zana had late-night debates about science and spirituality. But once the madness set in, respect vanished. He accused Zana of being sent by a demon and declared himself God, Creator and Shaper of Worlds. His brother Kirac would later blame Zana for consigning Baran to eternal madness.
cards.flavorText: "You seek the light, and you have found it. I am become God, Creator and Shaper of Worlds." — Baran

cards.title: Sirus, The Awakener
cards.text: Sirus survived his sacrifice against the Elder — trapped in glass, watching his friends leave. He returned incomplete, his essence stolen. For a subjective eternity he felt nothing — no joy, pain, or desire. He built a Map Device inside the Atlas to escape, creating a devastating storm. When Zana sealed the Atlas, she unknowingly condemned him to centuries of isolation.
cards.flavorText: "You left me there, Zana... centuries alone in the Atlas... all I wanted was to feel something again..." — Sirus, on his death

cards.title: The Envoy & The Maven
cards.text: When the Elder's silence echoed across the cosmos, new entities turned their gaze toward the Atlas. The Envoy — once a man, once a father — serves as guardian and prison for The Maven, a childlike cosmic entity bred to test the limits of limitless power. She escaped her cosmic prison when the Elder's silence deafened all sentries. She seeks conflict, collecting warriors as toys.
cards.flavorText: "She is but a petulant infant, subject to the whims of her desires and unaware of her own strength." — The Envoy

cards.title: The Citizen Vanguard & Kirac
cards.text: After Sirus devastated Oriath, the people evacuated to Karui Shores. Commander Kirac formed the Citizen Vanguard — ordinary volunteers tired of the endless parade of doom. Not soldiers, but families. They wage a secret celestial war in the Atlas, keeping eldritch threats occupied so they don't notice Wraeclast.
cards.flavorText: "We are the people's response to the madness of Wraeclast. We've had enough of corruption, gods, and would-be dictators." — Helena

cards.title: The Cleansing Fire & The Tangle
cards.text: Two cosmic entities arrived to challenge the Maven for the Atlas. The Cleansing Fire — a colossal brain of blazing suns and black stars — seeks omniscience, disintegrating everything it studies while keeping a library of trapped minds. The Tangle — a horrific mass of merged organic beings — eternally consumes and is consumed, each mouth desperate for escape from pain.
cards.flavorText: "The enemies outnumber the stars in the sky. The enemies are the stars in the sky." — The Envoy

cards.title: The Battle for the Atlas — Champions
cards.text: The Maven pitted her champion (the Exile) against champions of each entity. From the Cleansing Fire: The Black Star (a single neuron in a web of stars) and The Searing Exarch (who spread the Word of Enlightenment for eons). From the Tangle: The Infinite Hunger (a labyrinth of stomachs) and The Eater of Worlds (devouring worlds to satiate desperate masters).
cards.flavorText: "Champion against champion. So it must be." — The Maven

cards.title: The Maven's Victory
cards.text: The Exile defeated all four champions, solidifying the Maven's claim on the Atlas. But the Envoy warned: "This was merely the beginning." The enemies are countless. For now, the Maven controls the Atlas and is content to play — keeping Wraeclast safe by accident. Kirac acknowledges this is the best of terrible options.
cards.flavorText: "Oh, what a delight! We've won! The Atlas is ours. Now I can play with my best friend, forever." — The Maven

cards.title: Secrets of the Atlas — Eagon Caeserius
cards.text: Eagon Caeserius — Valdo's bastard son and Zana's half-brother — arrives at the Atlas. Raised by a foster family, he spent years uncovering his true lineage. He discovers that Zana is the 'Originator' — she has somehow entangled herself with the Atlas fabric, her memories spilling over and reshaping reality. Through tears in reality, Eagon and the Exile chase Zana through her memories.
cards.flavorText: "What I lack in sheer strength, I make up for with Caeserius wit and arrogance." — Eagon

cards.title: Zana's Plan & Farewell
cards.text: Pursuing Zana through memories of her loneliness, trauma, and reverence for her father, the Exile discovers Zana's desperate plan: she intends to weave herself permanently into the Atlas to guard it from within. Eagon tries to stop her, but Zana is resolute. In the end, she chooses sacrifice over reunion — becoming one with the Atlas to protect humanity from the cosmic threats that never stop coming.
cards.flavorText: "Perhaps the Atlas has eroded that part of me, as well." — Zana

timeline.title: Valdo Caeserius Releases The Elder
timeline.text: Chief Arkhon Valdo is deceived by the Elder's Shade while repairing the Map Device. High Templar Venarius forces them into the Dreamlands and pulls Starforge from the Elder's chest, freeing it. Valdo escapes with daughter Zana, then returns alone to fight.
timeline.flavorText: "My daughter... My darling daughter... By the gods. So much has transpired..." — Valdo, Book of Memories

timeline.title: The War for the Atlas
timeline.text: Zana rebuilds the Map Device and recruits five exiles: Sirus, Baran, Al-Hezmin, Drox, Veritania. They pursue the Shaper (Valdo's twisted form) and confront the Elder. Using the Cosmic Arcana, they seal the Elder — but Sirus is trapped with it.
timeline.flavorText: "Sirus leapt onto it. We saw the demon tap into his body... Both gone." — Baran's Journal

timeline.title: The Conquerors Go Mad
timeline.text: The Atlas erodes the minds of the remaining exiles. Al-Hezmin obsesses over being the best. Drox dreams of a kingdom. Veritania becomes contemptuous of all. Baran declares himself God. Zana seals the Atlas to stop them — trapping everyone, including Sirus who mysteriously returns, hollow and enraged.
timeline.flavorText: "The Atlas does strange things to one's thought processes... it's the Atlas itself. I'm sure of it." — Zana

timeline.title: Sirus Attacks Oriath — The Second Fall
timeline.text: Sirus escapes the Atlas and attacks Oriath in despair. The Exile and 800 Vanguard soldiers defeat him at great cost. Oriath is evacuated to Karui Shores. Zana, devastated by Sirus's death, walks off into the Atlas and disappears.
timeline.flavorText: "You left me there, Zana... centuries alone in the Atlas... all I wanted was to feel something again..." — Sirus

timeline.title: The Maven Arrives — Echoes of the Atlas
timeline.text: The Elder's silence draws cosmic attention. The Maven — a childlike eldritch entity — arrives with her guardian The Envoy to claim the Atlas as her playground. She collects warriors as toys, including the Conquerors, forcing them to fight endlessly for her amusement.
timeline.flavorText: "Conflict for my entertainment! Relieve my boredom. Kill for me." — The Maven

timeline.title: Siege of the Atlas — Cosmic War
timeline.text: Two cosmic entities — The Cleansing Fire and The Tangle — challenge the Maven for the Atlas. Kirac and the Citizen Vanguard ally with the Maven. The Exile defeats their champions: The Black Star, The Searing Exarch, The Infinite Hunger, The Eater of Worlds. The Maven wins — for now.
timeline.flavorText: "Two claimants have been turned away. But this was merely the beginning." — The Envoy

timeline.title: Secrets of the Atlas — Zana's Fate
timeline.text: Eagon Caeserius (Valdo's bastard son) discovers Zana is the Originator — her memories are reshaping the Atlas. Through memory tears, the Exile witnesses Zana's life. She plans to weave herself into the Atlas permanently, becoming its eternal guardian against cosmic threats.
timeline.flavorText: "Sweet sister... Do what you must, Exile. Save her from whatever horror the Atlas makes of her memory!" — Eagon

summary.title: Atlas of Worlds — Key Outcomes
items: ✅ The Elder sealed by Zana's team using the Cosmic Arcana
✅ Sirus sacrificed himself to trap the Elder, later returned hollow
✅ All four Conquerors fell to Atlas madness — trapped inside
✅ Sirus defeated after attacking Oriath — second evacuation
✅ The Maven claimed the Atlas, keeping cosmic threats occupied
✅ Champions of The Cleansing Fire & The Tangle defeated
✅ Eagon Caeserius discovered as Zana's half-brother
⚠️ Zana wove herself into the Atlas — her fate is the Atlas itself
⚠️ The Envoy warns: countless more entities will come
⚠️ The Maven is a childlike god — unpredictable and dangerous
